note: D = retained DJF station-days. mnwx begins D x 53; conversions add 3 cols to make D x 56. Quality filtering changes values without dropping these daily rows.
note: missing or rejected values cannot contribute. _q=False means no rejection flag recorded; it does not guarantee the measurement exists.
note: both TMAX and TMIN must exist. This estimates daily temperature from extremes; it is not an hourly mean. Daily averaging already weights the different month lengths correctly.
note: K represented station-winters replace D daily rows. station and winter_year become two index levels. Six aggregates = K x 6 data columns, before missing counts and classes.
note: precip / snow are summed within each winter, then winter totals are averaged later. min_count=1 prevents an entirely missing group from appearing as zero.
BUILDOUT: generalize expected days using actual season boundaries: DJF 90/91, MAM 92, JJA 92, SON 91. Keep daily averaging, or day-weight any monthly intermediate.
BUILDOUT: existing missing-day counts combine missing and quality-rejected measurements. Report those separately, with expected, raw, rejected and usable counts.
note: strict completeness applies separately to each metric. One missing / rejected day removes that seasonal metric. Other metrics from the same station-winter can remain valid.
note: station_winters is K x 11 after join: 3 metrics + 3 valid counts + 3 missing counts + 2 classes, indexed by station / winter_year. Inner join retains only class-table matches.

BUILDOUT: current code only displays. Save numerical tables, coverage / SD products and figures. Clean-run regenerated outputs are needed; saved notebook displays may be stale.

BUILDOUT: SD and sample sizes
No SD is calculated. Define it before coding: for each station / index / season / category, sample SD across accepted seasonal values is one candidate (ddof=1; missing if n<2).
For ensembles, distinguish year-to-year variability of the ensemble series from spread among station means. Do not average station SDs to get ensemble SD.
Expose missing-day columns and report accepted / excluded season counts per metric. A complete station x season x year grid must include wholly absent periods.

REQUIRED CHECKPOINT: exact Kenny table first
When implementing the reference output, ASK USER AGAIN to define variables, formulas, row / column layout, periods, geography, units, rounding, index version and appearance. This chart is not that approval.
Match the correct statewide / MSP source and weather window. DJF snowfall differs from a full snow-season total; a nine-station ensemble is not automatically a statewide average.
Validate and SAVE the exact reference table first. Then duplicate for every station individually, then build ensemble tables with the agreed weighting, SD and coverage outputs.

VERIFY before phase-one completion
Restart and run from frozen inputs. Check 1950 boundaries, seasonal keys, leap days, rounding / persistence, unknowns, whole absent seasons and quality handling.
Confirm any donor splices actually exist and retain provenance; the investigation notebook alone does not apply replacements.
These are descriptive weather means. SD is variability, not automatically confidence limits or evidence of causal ENSO effects. Nearby stations and episode-linked years are dependent.

note: monthly starts N x 2, one row for each retained station-day. This is repeated monthly information, not N independent index observations.

note: M x 1 series with monthly-period index. Missing calendar positions become NaN. A month absent from all retained station-days remains missing, even if the source index file contains it.
VERIFY: rounding can move borderline entries across thresholds and alters episode peaks. Compare year-by-year classifications against the same source / version.
note: 5 consecutive entries of an already-centered 3-month product. No new running average is computed. Missing values fail the threshold test.
note: shifts mark every member of each valid 5-entry window. Overlapping windows join into one episode. An episode may span several seasons or winters.
note: ID is unique per detected run within this index / phase call, not per yearly event. ONI warm, RONI warm and cold IDs are separate namespaces.

note: monthly series map back to N positions. Return is N x 3 with episode, episode_id, episode_peak. Daily row order is preserved; the input dataframe is not mutated here.

oni_classify(value) — definition, called on rounded entries or episode peaks
Missing -> NA
Strong El Nino: value >=1.5
Moderate El Nino: 1.0 <= value <=1.4
Weak El Nino: 0.5 <= value <=0.9
Neutral: -0.5 < value <0.5
Weak La Nina: -0.9 <= value <=-0.5
Moderate La Nina: -1.4 <= value <=-1.0
Strong La Nina: value <=-1.5
Else: Unclassified strength. No very-strong ONI class.

roni_classify(value) — ordered threshold checks
Missing -> NA
Very strong El Nino: >=2.0; strong: [1.5,2.0)
Moderate El Nino: [1.0,1.5); weak: [0.5,1.0)
Neutral: (-0.5,0.5)
Weak La Nina: (-1.0,-0.5]; moderate: (-1.5,-1.0]
Strong La Nina: (-2.0,-1.5]; very strong: <=-2.0
These strength functions do not themselves test persistence.
ONI strong and RONI strong cover different ranges; compare categories under explicitly matched definitions.
